Companion Animal Travel Desk page - Crate rules and fees matter because they protect animals, keep boarding smooth, and prevent last-minute changes that stress everyone involved. For new staff at Aurelia Skyways, your job starts with precise checks, clear communication, and safe handling on the day of travel. This page covers the two most common gate-stoppers: crate size limits and the standard travel fee for a cat.

First, confirm the crate can safely fit the animal. Measure the longest side of the crate against our published allowance, and ensure the crate is secure, well-ventilated, and clean. Think like an inspector: if the crate edges are misaligned, doors do not lock firmly, or the animal cannot stand and turn comfortably, escalation is required before the passenger reaches the boarding point. Place the animal and crate together only when the crate passes your check, and document any exceptions immediately so the senior coordinator can make decisions without delay. Here is the required crate-size check you must enforce: A cat crate may not exceed 61 cm, meaning the longest side of the crate.

Next, confirm payment and paperwork alignment. The travel fee must be assessed according to the animal type, and it must match what is recorded in the booking system and on the traveler’s documents. If the fee is missing, misapplied, or not collected before boarding, your welcome team must stop the flow and route the case for resolution. Keep the tone calm and the process fast; clear guidance reduces anxiety for travelers and prevents repeated questions at the desk. Here is the required fee rule you must apply: A cat travel fee is $85, meaning the charge for bringing a cat on this itinerary.

Throughout the day, coordinate with the safety coordinator for any concerns about hazards around the holding areas, ramps, or loading routes. Maintain a steady handoff between intake, staging, and boarding so Rosie and other traveling pets experience the same low-stress routine. Remember: verify crate size first, confirm the cat fee next, then escalate fast when either check fails.
